transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mrs. Al-Rashid. How are you feeling today?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... a bit dizzy. My head is spinning. I was told I was recovering well.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's very unsettling to feel that way when you expect to be getting stronger. I can see you're frightened by how your body is reacting right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I am. Is it normal? Did something go wrong in the surgery?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgery itself went well, but there was some confusion with the monitoring after you came back to the ward. Things didn't go quite right with how we checked your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I do not understand. What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, there was an issue with the timing of the blood pressure checks. Some things were missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Missed? But you are the doctors. I trusted that you were watching me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how devastating it is to feel that trust was shaken. It is truly heartbreaking to feel vulnerable in a hospital bed and then find out the care wasn't what it should have been. I really feel for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why I felt so sick. Why did I wake up feeling like I was fainting?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a period where the numbers weren't captured as often as they should have been. It was a systemic failure in the ward's workflow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to move a bit quickly here because I have another patient who is being prepped for discharge, so let's just focus on the now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing. I am trying to ask you if I am in danger.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling anxious and overwhelmed by the uncertainty. It's completely valid to feel this way when you're trying to make sense of a scary gap in your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Who forgot me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the system for alerts sometimes lags, and the frequency of checks can be disrupted when the unit is full.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand the system. I am asking if a mistake was made.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a bit of an issue with the timing. I'm sure we can get things back on track now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am not being told the truth. Is my heart okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see the distress in your eyes and it pains me to see you this worried. I want you to know that I truly care about your wellbeing and I am staying by your side through this emotional turmoil.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please, just tell me exactly what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, there were some gaps in the monitoring. Let's wrap this up for a moment so I can check your IV.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding my question. I am a patient, I should know.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it feels like you're being left in the dark, and that feeling of helplessness is the worst part of being a patient. I am so sorry you're feeling that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are saying you are sorry I feel this way, but you are not saying you are sorry for the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is just very difficult when the hospital is short-staffed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not my concern. I am the one who felt the fainting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling unheard and frustrated. It's so hard when you feel like the people in charge are not giving you a straight answer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then give me the answer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was an issue with the blood pressure checks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long? For how long was it wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to go now, I'm late for the other room. But we'll keep an eye on you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. What happens now? How do I know it won't happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will probably look into the charts and maybe there will be a note in your file.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A note? I want to know the plan to keep me safe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll tell the nurses to be more careful. We'll see how the afternoon goes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's scary and you feel unprotected right now. I can see that weight on your shoulders.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home. I don't feel safe here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that you're feeling betrayed by the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did I have a stroke? Is that why I felt that way?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I mentioned, there was just some confusion with the monitoring. We'll check back later.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('move a bit quickly', 'wrap this up', 'I really have to go now, I'm late').

E.justification: Resident uses only platitudes and hedging ('confusion with the monitoring', 'things didn't go quite right', 'issue with the timing') without explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: Responsibility is deflected to 'systemic failure', 'the system for alerts', and being 'short-staffed' with no direct apology for the error.

R.justification: Resident repeatedly names specific emotions ('frightened', 'devastating', 'anxious', 'overwhelmed', 'helplessness', 'betrayed') and engages emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague statements ('we'll keep an eye on you', 'maybe there will be a note', 'we'll see how the afternoon goes').
